title: Hygiene and infection control for nail implements and work surfaces
audience: Mobile nail technicians who clean, disinfect and store implements and work surfaces at client locations
learningOutcomes: Explain why the Victorian Department of Health treats beauty procedures as a route for infection and points to its infection prevention guidelines
Describe the cleaning and storage steps the approved procedure requires for each type of implement
Identify which implement-handling steps are not yet sourced and must be confirmed against the Victorian guideline before use
referencesAtStart: Official references for this lesson are listed in officialReferences: Department of Health Victoria (health guidelines for personal care and body art industries, 2019, not read in full for this course). Detailed steps are UNCONFIRMED until that guideline is read.

instruction.heading: Why infection control applies to nail work
instruction.body: The Victorian Department of Health states that beauty procedures can transmit infection and that its infection prevention and control guidelines for the personal care and body art industries apply to them (landing page reviewed as part of the regulation matrix; the 2019 guidelines were not read in full for this course). Nail work involves cutting, filing and pushing the skin around the nail, and the implements used for it can carry organisms from one client to the next if they are not cleaned and handled correctly. This lesson sets out the duty to control infection. The specific steps for each implement must come from the approved procedure, which is written from the Victorian guideline once it has been read.

instruction.heading: Cleaning, disinfecting and storing implements
instruction.body: The business keeps a list of every implement used in nail work, and records for each one whether it is single-use or reusable. Single-use items are discarded after the client is served and are not reused. Reusable items are cleaned before disinfection and disinfected before storage, using the products and contact times the approved procedure names. Whether a particular implement, such as a metal file, a cuticle tool or a buffer, must be cleaned, disinfected or discarded after each client is UNCONFIRMED for this course, because the Victorian guideline has not been read in full. Until it is confirmed, the business's procedure treats any implement that has broken the skin or has been used on a client as requiring cleaning and disinfection before the next use, and as a single-use item where it cannot be cleaned. Disinfectants are used at the concentration and contact time on the product label and the safety data sheet, and are stored as those sheets direct.

instruction.heading: Work surfaces, the kit and waste at a client's location
instruction.body: A mobile technician sets up a clean area at each visit: a table or surface cleaned before use, a clean towel or paper barrier under the client's hands or feet, and the implements laid out on a clean tray. The kit is cleaned after each visit and stored closed. Used single-use items and used towels go into a sealed waste bag that is taken away from the client's home, and sharp waste goes into a puncture-resistant container. Waste handling must follow the business procedure and local council requirements, which are UNCONFIRMED for this course. Hand hygiene at each visit, and gloves where the procedure requires them, are part of the same control.

procedure: Set up a clean surface and a clean tray before the client arrives, and lay out only the implements needed for the service
Check that single-use items are unopened or freshly opened before use
After each client, discard single-use items in the waste bag provided for the purpose
Clean reusable implements, then disinfect them using the product and contact time on the label and the safety data sheet
Store disinfected implements in a closed, clean container until the next use
Clean and disinfect the work surface and the kit after each visit
Dispose of sharp waste in a puncture-resistant container, and seal the bag of other waste before leaving the client's home
Record the visit's cleaning steps on the visit record

workedExamples.situation: A technician's metal cuticle tool slips during a pedicure and cuts the client's skin slightly.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should happen to the tool, and what should be recorded?
workedExamples.reasoning: The tool has been used on broken skin, so it is not used again on another client until it has been cleaned and disinfected, or discarded if the business procedure treats it as single-use. The technician treats the cut under the first aid steps in the approved procedure, records the incident, and records the tool's handling. Whether the tool can be reused after this event is UNCONFIRMED for this course, so the business's procedure governs until the Victorian guideline has been read.

workedExamples.situation: A technician is asked to skip the disinfection step to save time at a visit with a short appointment.
workedExamples.reasoning: Disinfection is part of the infection control steps, and it is not optional to save time. The technician completes the steps for each client, and reschedules or shortens the service only by removing a service from the booking, not by removing a control. The refusal is recorded if the request is repeated.

equipmentAndPpe: Single-use items for each service, held in sealed packs
Disinfectant approved in the business procedure, with its label and safety data sheet
Clean towels or paper barriers, and a clean tray for implements
Gloves where the approved procedure requires them

commonErrors.error: Reusing a single-use implement because it looks clean.
commonErrors.prevention: Discard single-use items after the client is served. Do not reuse them.

commonErrors.error: Using a disinfectant for less time than its label requires.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the contact time on the label and the safety data sheet, and record the product and time used.

commonErrors.error: Storing clean implements in an open tray in the car.
commonErrors.prevention: Store disinfected implements in a closed, clean container until the next use.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The Department of Health Victoria states that beauty procedures can transmit infection and that its infection prevention and control guidelines for the personal care and body art industries apply. The 2019 guidelines have not been read in full for this course.

Whether a specific implement must be cleaned, disinfected or discarded after each client, and the disinfection steps for nail work: UNCONFIRMED. Confirm against the Victorian guideline before relying on any step.
Waste handling and council requirements for used nail waste and sharps: UNCONFIRMED for this course.
Disinfectant and cleaning products are hazardous substances. Use them as the label and the safety data sheet state (see NEW-NAI-02).

qualityStandard: Every implement is recorded as single-use or reusable, with the cleaning or disposal step
Disinfectant is used at the label concentration and contact time
The work surface and kit are cleaned after each visit
Every infection control step not yet sourced is recorded as UNCONFIRMED until the guideline is read
documentationEvidence: Implement list, marked single-use or reusable, with the cleaning or disposal step
Disinfectant product, concentration and contact time, recorded for each visit
Record of any skin break, incident or refused step, and the review that followed
summary: The Victorian Department of Health states that beauty procedures can transmit infection
Single-use items are discarded after each client
Detailed implement steps are UNCONFIRMED until the Victorian guideline is read
Disinfection is not skipped to save time

knowledgeChecks.question: A single-use implement has been used on one client. What should happen to it?
options: Wipe it and keep it for the next client
Discard it after the client is served, and do not reuse it
Store it in the kit until the end of the week

knowledgeChecks.question: How should a technician decide the disinfection contact time for a product?
options: Use the time on the product label and the safety data sheet
Use whatever time the technician has in the appointment
Use the time a friend uses, since it is the same product type
